lines.text: My father stood in Greyhollow's yard with snow on his shoulders, looking at the keep.
Fifteen years, and Bram still hasn't fixed that gutter.
Fifteen years? You've never been here.
I've been here, Lucan. Walk with me.
He walked straight to the walled garden behind the keep, the one Bram kept locked. I'd always assumed it was the wine. Inside: a stone bench, and dead, thorny stems.
Roses. She grew roses here. In the north. Nobody else could ever make them grow.
Her name was Elinor.
She was hollow-born, like you. I found her half frozen on the north road, running from the Order. I hid her in the coldest place I owned. Here.
I had a wife and a son, and I loved her anyway. That part I won't ask you to forgive.
You were born upstairs, in the room with the round window, in a snowstorm.
I sat down on the bench. My legs decided for me.
That same winter, Lady Isolde died in childbed. Her baby died with her. A little boy. He lived one night.
So I told the world Isolde's son had lived, and been sent north to a wet nurse. And I buried her boy here, under a stone with no name.
Two lies and one grave. That was how I kept you.
For two years your mother nursed her own son in this garden, and everyone thought she was the wet nurse.
Then her roses bloomed in the snow, and a Measurer passing through saw them.
When the Order came, you were two. She told them her baby was born dead, and showed them the grave. They believed a grave. They took her, and never knew you were there.
I raised you as Isolde's, at arm's length, so no one would look twice. At least the boy is honest. I said it so the hall would laugh, and nobody would think.
And I sent you north, because the cold hides what you are. And because Bram was here.
The woman under the cathedral. The one who knew my name.
Your mother. Yes.
I think I had known, somewhere underneath, since she said I'd got tall. But knowing and being told are different kinds of cold.
Why didn't you tell me?
Because a boy who knows what he is acts like it. You had to believe you were nothing. It kept you alive.
I went to find Bram. He was sitting on the garden steps in the snow, as if he'd been waiting.
Sit down, my lord. It's a long story, and I'm the only one left who was there that night.
The Lord Who Measured Zero. Chapter one hundred and thirty-three, coming soon.
